name: Rejuran HB

lead: Rejuran HB is a polynucleotide injectable used in aesthetic clinics as a skin booster. People use it for smoother, healthier-looking skin texture and quality.

Polynucleotides are chains of nucleotides, and skin booster products inject them into the skin, where they are generally described as supporting repair and hydration. Rejuran products are referred to in the literature as a family that includes Rejuran S and Rejuran HB Plus. The only published study identified is a rabbit experiment on accidental arterial injection, and no human trials of Rejuran HB were found.

paras: A clinician injects it into the skin, typically as a short series of sessions. People use it as a skin-quality treatment rather than for volume.
The rabbit study examined vascular behavior of polynucleotide products after accidental intra-arterial exposure. Human safety data were not found in the sources reviewed.

angle.text: People use Rejuran HB as a skin booster for smoother, more even skin quality. Injected polynucleotides are described as supporting skin repair and hydration. Published human data for this product are very limited.

lead: Rejuran HB is a polynucleotide (PN) injectable used in aesthetic medicine as a skin booster, injected into the skin for a smoother, more hydrated and firmer-looking complexion. One Japanese clinic describes it as combining salmon-derived polynucleotide with hyaluronic acid, with the hyaluronic acid giving an immediate sense of hydration and the polynucleotide behind longer-term changes in firmness and texture.[1] Polynucleotides are chains of nucleotides, and the term covers DNA and RNA, which also have uses beyond cosmetics.[2]

The same clinic distinguishes standard Rejuran (polynucleotide only, aimed at overall skin quality), Rejuran S (a higher concentration, aimed at focused work on scars and uneven areas) and HB (with hyaluronic acid). It says HB may help firmness, pore appearance, fine lines and skin texture by supporting the skin's own collagen and elastin, and that it does not address sagging, deep wrinkles, deep acne scars or pigment spots.[1]

Published research on Rejuran HB itself is limited to a 2026 controlled rabbit study of what happens when polynucleotide products, including Rejuran S, Rejuran HB Plus and Conjuran, are accidentally injected into an artery.[3] No human clinical trial of Rejuran HB was found.

One Japanese clinic says it is not approved as a pharmaceutical product in Japan [1]

paras: Skin boosters are injectables placed into the skin to improve hydration and quality rather than to add volume to a specific area. Rejuran HB is described by clinics as a polynucleotide booster with added hyaluronic acid, which the clinic says makes injections feel less painful and gives immediate hydration.[1]

One clinic says HB is intended for firmness, pores, fine lines and texture, suggests an initial series of three to four sessions three to four weeks apart followed by maintenance every three to six months, and says firmness and texture changes usually show from the second or third session.[1]

The clinic reports that small bumps at the injection sites usually settle within hours to a day, that bruising, if it occurs, can take about a week to fade and is more likely around the eyes and neck, and that makeup is often allowed the next day.[1]
The clinic lists redness, swelling, bruising, pain, small lumps, infection and allergic reactions, and advises people with fish allergies to disclose this because the ingredient is salmon-derived.[1]

A 2026 rabbit study was motivated by the increasing use of polynucleotide injectables and the need to understand their behaviour if injected into a blood vessel; its findings cannot be directly applied to humans.[3]

No studies found in humans. A 2026 controlled rabbit study in Scientific Reports compared intra-arterial injection of PN products of differing viscosity, including Rejuran S, Rejuran HB Plus and Conjuran, with saline and cross-linked hyaluronic acid, examining arterial flow and cutaneous consequences.[3]
